Cc: billing@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy in AWS Marketplace invoicing — apparent duplicate cumulative usage

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a strange line on our March AWS Marketplace statement that looks like cumulative usage recorded against two different Acme legal entities (EU and UK). The marketplace metering report attached shows the same subscription rendered twice under separate entity IDs and AWS is issuing invoices that split VAT incorrectly as a result.

Attached: AMZ-Marketplace-usage-report-202703.pdf and our internal comparison sheet Acme-invoice-comparison-202703.xlsx.

Can Redwood confirm whether you submitted two metering records for our deployment or if this is an AWS metering consolidation issue? This is preventing our AP team from approving payment — they need an agreed reconciliation or credit before we can release the payout.

Best,
Liam
Billing Lead, Acme Corp
liam@acme-corp.com

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discrepancy in AWS Marketplace invoicing — initial findings

Folks — quick update after pulling the metering submission logs and matching them to AWS events.

Findings (preliminary):
- Redwood submitted a single metering record for Acme account (subscription id sub_67X) on 2027-03-31 at 23:59:58 UTC.
- AWS consolidated billing shows two invoice line items because the subscription was mapped to two separate seller-entity IDs at AWS Marketplace (seller_entity_eu / seller_entity_uk). The raw event timestamps at AWS are identical, suggesting a mapping/attribution issue at the AWS side rather than duplicate metering from us.
- The VAT calculation on the two invoices uses different entity tax profiles which is why Acme sees a net/net mismatch.

Action items I initiated:
- Vanessa opened AWS Support case #123456789 and requested the raw seller-entity mapping logs and the origin of entity attribution.
- I'll prepare a provisional credit memo equal to the net of the duplicate line item (excluding VAT) so Acme's AP can process payment.

Estimate: 2 business days to get AWS response; credit memo ready by EOD today and I'll loop legal for signoff.

Marcus Lin
Manager, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discrepancy in AWS Marketplace invoicing — resolution and next steps

Hi Liam — thanks for your patience. AWS responded to our support case this morning. Summary and next steps below.

Resolution summary:
- AWS confirmed the duplicate invoice lines were caused by an internal seller-entity remapping that affected a subset of subscriptions during finalization; Redwood's metering submission was correctly single-sent for sub_67X.
- AWS will void invoice INV-AW-33981 (the duplicate line) and reissue a corrected consolidated invoice within 5 business days.
- AWS has issued a temporary holdback on the duplicate amount; they confirmed no immediate penalty but recommended coordination for VAT correction.

What Redwood will do now:
- Marcus has issued a provisional credit memo (CM-RED-2027-041) for the net duplicate amount; we will share the credit memo file with your AP for payment processing.
- Karthik (tax) is copied for VAT reallocation guidance — he will provide a one-off VAT reconciliation note you can include with your records.
- We'll monitor AWS case and confirm when the corrected invoice is posted; once posted we'll reconcile the credit memo against the corrected invoice in our ledger and share confirmation.

Please confirm that your AP will accept the provisional credit (CM-RED-2027-041) so we can send the document today. If you prefer to wait for the reissued AWS invoice before payment, let us know — that will delay funds by the correction window.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplaces Program Manager
Redwood Inference
